> Chaotic File Markup Language: a configuration language that accidentally became a scripting language, then a runtime, then a meme.

The foundation. Everything downstream depends on this being solid.

"""
CFML Lexer — turns raw source text into a flat list of Tokens.
"""

from __future__ import annotations
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum, auto


class TT(Enum):
    """Token types."""
    # Literals
    NUMBER      = auto()
    STRING      = auto()
    BOOL        = auto()
    # Names / directives
    IDENTIFIER  = auto()
    DIRECTIVE   = auto()   # @word
    # Structural
    LBRACKET    = auto()   # [
    RBRACKET    = auto()   # ]
    LBRACE      = auto()   # {
    RBRACE      = auto()   # }
    PIPE        = auto()   # |
    COMMA       = auto()   # ,
    COLON       = auto()   # :
    INDENT      = auto()   # -- prefix (block body marker)
    NEWLINE     = auto()
    EOF         = auto()


@dataclass
class Token:
    type: TT
    value: object          # str | int | float | bool | None
    line: int

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Token({self.type.name}, {self.value!r}, line={self.line})"


class LexError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, msg: str, line: int):
        super().__init__(f"[line {line}] LexError: {msg}")
        self.line = line

# Chaotic File Markup Language (CFML)

> "A configuration language that accidentally became a scripting language, then a runtime, then a meme."

## Philosophy

CFML was originally designed to avoid the complexity of JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, INI, and other sensible formats.

Instead of using explicit assignment operators:

```txt
5 X
```

CFML determines intent through contextual analysis.

Or, as the specification states:

> The parser shall figure it out.

---

# Core Features

## Variables

```txt
5 X
```

Assigns:

```txt
X = 5
```

depending on causality settings.

---

## Execution Direction

```txt
left-to-right true
```

Normal assignment behavior.

```txt
left-to-right false
```

Reverse assignment behavior.

```txt
left-to-right arbitrary
```

The parser engages in comparative analysis and attempts to determine user intent.

---

## Expressions

All expressions are prefix-based.

```txt
@eq X 5
```

Checks equality.

```txt
@neg @eq X 5
```

Negates equality result.

---

## Grouping

Single-value grouping:

```txt
{@eq X 5}
```

Multi-value grouping:

```txt
|X Y Z|
```

---

## Arrays

```txt
[1, 2, 3]
```

Standard array literal.

---

# Input / Output

## User Input

```txt
@get Name
```

Reads user input.

---

## Logging

```txt
@log Name
```

Outputs a value.

---
